name: Aurobindo Ghosh
role: Indian nationalist leader (1905-1910), later yogi and philosopher (1872-1950)
summary: Aurobindo was an early leader of the Indian nationalist movement who demanded complete autonomy, boycott and passive resistance (with armed revolt among the legitimate options), and after 1910 withdrew to Pondicherry to develop Integral Yoga. His political writings describe nationalism as a spiritual calling, warn against totalitarian collectivism and the sufficiency of reason, favour free self-determination of nations within an eventual world-union, and support the Allied cause in the Second World War.

allow-dual-citizenship.rationale: He suggested that dual or multilateral citizenship may appear and be compatible with national feeling, but as a possibility, not a programme.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: He wrote that armed revolt is one justified form of resistance to a foreign despotism, depending on circumstances.

change-traditions-that-no-longer-suit.rationale: He called the treatment of outcastes dishonouring to Indian culture and said caste degenerated into a chaos of evils now to be eliminated.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He rejected rule by a foreign bureaucracy and demanded autonomy free of British control, calling the alien bureaucracy a despotism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He called the war of classes an accident of socialism's birth and explained social development through psychological stages instead.

clerical-rule.rationale: He wrote that true theocracy is the kingdom of God in man, not the rule of a Pope, priesthood or sacerdotal class.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He argued that India's management lay with a people whose trade interests were opposed to India's, and campaigned against this.

communal-electorates.rationale: In Karmayogin he called separate Muslim representation an ill-advised measure and backed the Nationalist rejection of separate electorates.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: He called unbridled competition a parasitical excrescence yet wrote that no real step forward is made without struggle.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: He described commercialism, the accumulation of possessions and show, as a life devoid of beauty and nobility, and a burden crushing mankind.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He described the dictatorship of the proletariat as in fact the dictatorship of the Communist party and a rigorous totalitarianism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He welcomed the United Nations as a step toward a world-body and urged no pessimism about its defects.

free-trade.rationale: He told a 1908 audience that Britain pushed free trade for its own gain and that other countries, India included, could not accept it.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: In his speeches he presented the motherland as a divinity to be served and defended, not just land.

human-decline-since-golden-age.rationale: His Human Cycle describes humanity moving through evolving stages toward a spiritual age, not a long decline.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: In 1949 he said spirituality cannot be affirmed in a political constitution and declined to write it into one.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: His account of social development rests on psychological stages (infrarational, rational, spiritual), not on modes of production.

national-rebirth.rationale: He wrote of a long decline of Indian culture and called for its evolution toward the Vedic and Vedantic ideal, a renewal rather than only a recovery.

national-self-determination.rationale: He made free self-determination of peoples the basis of a coming world-union and, in Bande Mataram, demanded absolute autonomy for India.

party-controls-media.rationale: He counted full freedom of speech, thought and association as a gain of modern democracy worth keeping and noted it was suspended in Russia.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: He wrote that Indian society trained women less than men and gave them little escape from family control that men had.

person-over-state.rationale: He wrote that cooperative action is injurious if it immolates the individual to a communal egoism.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: He described the Second World War as a battle between evolutionary forces and diabolical values, and Allied victory as necessary for mankind's future.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: His 1947 message foresaw nationalism fulfilling itself in international institutions and a unification of mankind, which the nations need for their security.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: His Renaissance in India writings make survival of Indian culture on its spiritual basis a central aim.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He argued that reason is an insufficient, often inefficient guide for humanity and that the spirit must lead.

religious-nation.rationale: He called the idea of two nationalities in India a new-fangled notion and said Indian Muslims belong to the Indian nation as much as Hindus, though a 1909 speech tied the nation to the Sanatana Dharma.

restore-past-order.rationale: He held that Indian culture must evolve, not merely revive or prolong the Puranic system.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: In his 1947 message and 1949 notes he said the partition of India must go and rejected any lasting division into two federations.

right-to-secede.rationale: He called the breakup into separate States a disastrous relapse and held that India's division must end.

sacred-nation.rationale: He told Nationalists that Nationalism is a religion that has come from God, and that the nation is a divine Mother.

single-official-language.rationale: He held that a common language unites only when it is natural to a people and criticised the overshadowing of Indian tongues by English.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Human Cycle ends in a spiritual stage of society and holds that the spiritual is the truth behind all other human aims.

state-harmful.rationale: He held the State necessary at present while treating an anarchic freedom from compulsion as a distant truth for the future.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: In 1942 he publicly backed the Cripps offer so that India and Britain could stand united against the Axis.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He valued freedom of thought, speech and association and criticised its suppression in Russia, and in Bande Mataram opposed bureaucratic repression of dissent.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: In a 1908 speech he said Swadeshi brings in preference and protection for Indian goods and that an Indian-controlled government would put a heavy duty on English tea.

total-state.rationale: He warned that the State idea crushes everything in its way and that collective action which immolates the individual is injurious.

traditional-family.rationale: He called the joint-family order secure and workable for those who fit it, but said it leaves little room for individual will, especially for women.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He described democratic individualism as degenerating into an open or veiled plutocracy that shocks by its grossness and bankrupts the rational age.

notes: Based on the maintainer-supplied Complete Works volumes (25, 6-7, 8, 19, 20, 35). Themes searched: economy and socialism, state and government, democracy and speech, religion and state, nationalism and self-determination, empire, world-union, war and violence, caste and women, language, culture, spirituality. After 1910 he kept out of day-to-day politics, so most economic, criminal-justice, gender-identity, immigration and technology statements are null. His 1908 words on armed resistance are words only; he was acquitted at Alipore and has no record of violence.
